messages:
Priya (eng-arch): Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to refactor the tenant geofence handshake so control-plane consent is cached at edge proxies for a short TTL. Goal: reduce cross-region roundtrips during write path without breaking residency guarantees. Thoughts?
Luca (infra): sounds promising. main concern is stale consent leading to accidental cross-region writes. what's the TTL you have in mind?
Priya (eng-arch): thinking 30s-2m, adjustable per-tenant. handshake would still require an authoritative refresh on eviction or explicit revocation.
Noah (sre): we need a clear operator escape hatch. If an edge proxy caches a revoked consent, we must be able to force immediate invalidation cluster-wide. How do we broadcast that?
Priya (eng-arch): plan: control plane emits a revocation event to the routing bus; edge proxies subscribe and invalidate cache entries immediately. fallback if bus partitioned: proxies fall back to synchronous consent check.
Maya (product): user-visible impact? The product requirement is zero-residency-leak in normal ops. We prefer short window for caches; customers can opt-in for aggressive caching at their own risk.
Luca (infra): implementation notes: add a consent cache layer in proxy, keyed by tenant-id+region. On miss or after invalidation marker, proxy does sync call to control-plane endpoint: /v1/consent/check.
Priya (eng-arch): sample header we propose to add: 
``
x-tenant-id: <id>
x-tenant-geofence: <region-tag>
x-consent-cache-ttl: <ms>
```
Luca (infra): +1 to header approach. Make sure we sign the header or only accept from trusted proxies.
Noah (sre): telemetry: we need metrics for cache-hit-rate, stale-invalidations, and any sync fallbacks. also track cross-region-write attempts while cached.
Priya (eng-arch): agreed. add three new metrics: geofence_cache_hit, geofence_forced_invalidation, geofence_sync_fallback_count. set alert if fallback_count/tps > 0.1% over 5m.
Maya (product): can we build an admin toggle per-tenant in the console to enable/disable caching? legal/regulatory teams will want that.
Priya (eng-arch): yes — toggle + per-tenant TTL override. default: off for any tenant with a residency flag. default on for others with conservative TTL 30s.
Luca (infra): rollouts: implement feature-flag gated on proxy side. start with internal tenants in staging -> canary -> global. We need migration plan for proxies that don't understand the header (backwards compatibility).
Priya (eng-arch): compatibility: if proxy doesn't send header, control-plane behaves as before. if control-plane responds with 200+consent=true and a cache TTL, proxy may cache; older proxies ignore TTL header.
Noah (sre): runbook: if we see cross-region write errors spike, operator steps: 1) flip off consent-cache FF 2) issue global invalidation 3) revert proxies if needed. docs + playbook required.
Maya (product): timeline? customers want measurable latency reduction for small chat workloads. can we measure expected p50 token latency improvement?
Luca (infra): estimate: avoid one RTT to control-plane per request — ~20-40ms saved p50 in EU->US cases. batching and KV cache still bigger wins, but this helps for cold requests.
Priya (eng-arch): next actions: 1) write short RFC with API sketch + header contract 2) infra spike for proxy cache implementation 3) telemetry plan + alerts 4) staging run with internal tenants. volunteers to own?
Luca (infra): I can take proxy spike.
Noah (sre): I'll draft telemetry and runbook.
Maya (product): I'll scope console toggle and customer comms.
Priya (eng-arch): I'll write RFC draft and API contract. tagging deploy-bot to schedule canary window. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary window scheduled: 2024-11-02T18:00:00Z -> 2024-11-09T18:00:00Z. Change owner: Priya.
Luca (infra): cool — will post progress updates here as we hit infra checkpoints.
Noah (sre): adding a checklist item: chaos test that simulates control-plane bus partition and validate fallbacks.
Priya (eng-arch): good call. thanks everyone. will share RFC link once draft is in docs.
